title: feat(search,core): add fuzzy search and plugin event bus
body:
## Summary / 摘要

Add fzf-style fuzzy search to the search plugin (P2 #17) and a plugin
event bus to the core (P2 #10). The demo search bar now includes a
"Fuzzy" toggle and a match counter.

## Motivation / 背景与动机

- Roadmap: items 17 (fuzzy search) and 10 (plugin event bus)
- OpenSpec: add-search-fuzzy, add-plugin-event-bus

## Changes / 变更内容

- packages/core:
  - Add PluginEventBus + EditorAPI.getEventBus()
  - Add onInit hook to NexusPlugin
  - Core emits document.change, focus, blur, selection.change
- packages/plugin-search:
  - Add fuzzy option + buildFuzzyPattern() + fuzzyScore()
  - Add Fuzzy checkbox and match counter to search panel
- apps/electron-demo:
  - Add Fuzzy checkbox to demo search bar

## Testing / 测试

- pnpm test — 558 tests pass (no regressions)
- pnpm build for both core and plugin-search passes
- Manual: demo search bar fuzzy toggle finds "hello" from "hlo"

## Compliance / 合规自检

- [x] No new runtime dependencies
- [x] No build artifacts / secrets committed
- [x] Change aligns with project scope (P2 roadmap items)

@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+# Change: Add Plugin Event Bus
+
+## Why
+Plugins currently have no way to communicate with each other. The
+Outline panel only refreshes on manual toggle, Backlinks don't react
+to file switches, and every plugin must poll the EditorAPI. A shared
+event bus lets plugins broadcast and listen for typed events, enabling
+reactive cross-plugin communication without tight coupling.
+
+## What Changes
+- Add a `PluginEventBus` class (wraps `EventEmitter`) to `packages/core`
+- Expose `getEventBus()` on `EditorAPI` so plugins can access the bus
+- Add `onInit?: (api: EditorAPI) => void` to `NexusPlugin` — called after
+  editor construction so plugins can subscribe to events
+- Plugins import and call `definePluginEvent<T>(name)` to register typed events
+  with payload interfaces, enabling type-safe emit/listen in TypeScript
+- Core emits built-in events: `document.change`, `file.open`, `focus`,
+  `blur`, `selection.change`
+- Zero new runtime dependencies
+
+## Impact
+- Affected specs: `core` (new capability: plugin-event-bus)
+- Affected code: `packages/core/src/event-emitter.ts`,
+  `packages/core/src/editor.ts`, `packages/core/src/types.ts`
+- No breaking changes — `onInit` is optional, event bus is additive

@@ -0,0 +1,43 @@
+## ADDED Requirements
+### Requirement: Plugin Event Bus
+The editor core SHALL provide a shared event bus accessible to all plugins
+via `EditorAPI.getEventBus()`. Plugins MAY emit typed events and subscribe
+to events from other plugins or from the core.
+
+#### Scenario: Plugin subscribes to document change event
+- **WHEN** a plugin calls `bus.on("document.change", handler)` in `onInit`
+- **THEN** the handler SHALL be called with the new document string and AST
+  every time the document content changes
+
+#### Scenario: Plugin emits a custom event
+- **WHEN** a plugin calls `bus.emit("myPlugin.ready", { status: "loaded" })`
+- **THEN** any subscriber to `"myPlugin.ready"` SHALL receive the payload
+
+#### Scenario: Unsubscribing stops event delivery
+- **WHEN** a plugin calls `bus.off("event.name", handler)`
+- **THEN** the removed handler SHALL NOT be called on subsequent emits
+
+### Requirement: Plugin Initialization Hook
+The `NexusPlugin` interface SHALL support an optional `onInit` callback
+that receives the `EditorAPI` instance. This hook is called after the
+editor is fully constructed, giving plugins access to the event bus and
+editor API for subscription setup.
+
+#### Scenario: Plugin subscribes in onInit
+- **WHEN** a plugin defines `onInit(api)` that calls `api.getEventBus().on(...)`
+- **THEN** the subscription SHALL be active for the editor's lifetime
+
+### Requirement: Built-in Core Events
+The editor core SHALL emit the following events on the plugin event bus:
+
+| Event | Payload | When |
+|-------|---------|------|
+| `document.change` | `{ doc: string, ast: Root }` | Document content changes |
+| `focus` | `{}` | Editor gains focus |
+| `blur` | `{}` | Editor loses focus |
+| `selection.change` | `{ anchor: number, head: number }` | Selection changes |
+
+#### Scenario: Core event is emitted on change
+- **WHEN** the user types a character in the editor
+- **THEN** `document.change` event SHALL be emitted on the plugin event bus
+  with the updated document string and AST

@@ -0,0 +1,24 @@
+# Change: Add fuzzy search to plugin-search
+
+## Why
+The existing regexp/whole-word/case-sensitive options require typing exact
+substrings. Users who mis-type or only remember fragments of a word get zero
+results. Fuzzy matching (fzf-style character-order matching) lets users find
+"hello" by typing "hlo", dramatically improving search UX.
+
+## What Changes
+- Add `fuzzy` option to `SearchOptions` and `SearchPluginOptions`
+- Implement zero-dependency fuzzy matching that scores and converts a user
+  query into a CodeMirror-compatible `RegExp`
+- Add a "Fuzzy" checkbox toggle to the search-panel UI (alongside match-case /
+  regexp / whole-word)
+- Public API: `buildFuzzyPattern(query: string, options?: SearchOptions): RegExp | null`
+- Public API: `fuzzyScore(query: string, candidate: string): number`
+- When `fuzzy` is on, `regexp` and `wholeWord` are ignored (mutually exclusive)
+
+## Impact
+- Affected specs: `search`
+- Affected code: `packages/plugin-search/src/index.ts`,
+  `packages/plugin-search/test/`
+- No breaking changes — `fuzzy` defaults to `false`
+- Zero new runtime dependencies

@@ -0,0 +1,36 @@
+## ADDED Requirements
+### Requirement: Fuzzy Search
+The search plugin SHALL support fuzzy matching when the `fuzzy` option is
+enabled. In fuzzy mode, the user's query characters are matched in order
+against candidate text with any gaps allowed, and the resulting match spans
+are converted into a valid regular expression usable by CodeMirror's search
+cursor.
+
+#### Scenario: Fuzzy match finds results with gaps
+- **WHEN** the document contains "hello world" and the user searches "hlo"
+  with `fuzzy: true`
+- **THEN** "hello" is matched because 'h', 'l', 'o' appear in order
+
+#### Scenario: Fuzzy match fails on wrong order
+- **WHEN** the document contains "hello" and the user searches "olh"
+  with `fuzzy: true`
+- **THEN** no match is returned because characters are out of order
+
+#### Scenario: Fuzzy exact match scores highest
+- **WHEN** the document contains "hello" and the user searches "hello"
+  with `fuzzy: true`
+- **THEN** "hello" is matched with the maximum possible score
+
+#### Scenario: Fuzzy mutually exclusive with regexp and wholeWord
+- **WHEN** `fuzzy: true` is set
+- **THEN** the `regexp` and `wholeWord` options SHALL be ignored
+
+#### Scenario: Fuzzy toggle in search panel UI
+- **WHEN** the search panel is open
+- **THEN** a "Fuzzy" checkbox SHALL be visible alongside Match Case, Regexp,
+  and By Word toggles
+- **AND** checking it SHALL switch the search to fuzzy mode
+
+#### Scenario: Reset fuzzy state on panel close
+- **WHEN** the search panel is closed and reopened
+- **THEN** the fuzzy checkbox SHALL reset to its default (off)
